analysis.title: TFI International (TFII.TO) 3Q26 EPS Miss Due To Weaker LTL Profits; Lowering Forecast on LTL; Logistics and TL Performing Well
key_insights: TFII reported 3Q26 recurring EPS of $1.67, below GS estimate of $1.76 and Visible Alpha consensus of $1.75.
4Q26 EPS guide of $1.30-$1.40 is below GS forecast of $1.60 and consensus of $1.63. The guide assumes no significant positive or negative change in the operating environment.
The miss came from US LTL, where the turnaround to consistent profitability and y/y margin improvement is not yet happening. Truckload and Logistics continue to perform well.

LTL revenue was 3% below GS estimate. LTL operating ratio (OR) was 91.3% vs GS 89.5%, a 180bps miss, because higher costs stayed in the network after TFI priced out lower-yielding 3PL shipments gained in 2Q26 without getting higher revenue per shipment in 3Q26.
LTL yields ex-fuel were down 1% (GSe down 0.5%), shipments per day rose 5% (GSe +4%), tonnage rose 1% (GSe +3%) and weight per shipment fell 4%.

Truckload OR was 86.7% vs GS 85.5%, a 120bps miss, but still within management's 550-650bps y/y OR improvement guidance (about 560bps y/y). Logistics OR was 88.7% vs GS 88.5%, with EBIT $9mn above GS at $49mn.
GS expects LTL fixes to take time across price, cost and service. Density needs to build to offset cost inflation, and a firmer manufacturing environment would help.
Management plans to bring in an outside manager to work on the LTL turnaround.

The 6-year UPS Ground Freight Pricing (GFP) reseller deal ends in January 2027. GS estimates this removes about $120mn of LTL revenue and $16mn of EBIT, or about $0.15 per share, and includes it in the estimate cut.
4Q26 segment OR guide (y/y): LTL worse by 0-100bps, Truckload better by 400-500bps, Logistics better by 100-200bps. LTL OR would improve sequentially by 40-140bps as 3PL surge costs exit.
Management says freight demand is muted. Capacity reductions are lifting truckload rates while LTL stays weak with the industrial economy.
GS cuts EPS estimates to $5.56 for 2026 (from $5.90), $7.05 for 2027 (from $7.55) and $8.15 for 2028 (from $8.65). It expects LTL margin to stay under pressure in 1H27.

Price target cut to $155 from $178 (C$211 from C$242), based on 19.5x P/E (from 22.0x) on Q5-Q8 EPS of $7.98. The multiple was cut in line with other LTL carriers and for added discount to peers over turnaround timing.
Buy rating maintained. GS needs more visibility on timing and pace of the LTL turnaround to be comfortable with the longer-term growth path.
Management says it could deploy $1-1.5bn on acquisitions in US LTL or Logistics if the right opportunity arises. FY2026 net capex guide of $225-250mn is unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: Buy kept after the 3Q26 miss and weak 4Q guide. Target multiple cut to 19.5x from 22.0x on uncertain timing of the US LTL turnaround. Implies 37.7% upside from $112.54.

sector_views.rationale: LTL remains weak with the industrial economy and the industry is moving off a bottom in tonnage. Truckload rates are being helped by capacity reductions, and flatbed exposure and Logistics are bright spots.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 recurring EPS reported $1.67 vs GS estimate $1.76 and Visible Alpha consensus $1.75 (reported 10/29/2026 print, covered 10/30).
3Q26 total revenue $1,857.9mn vs GS estimate $1,870.1mn (-1%). The consensus table shows $2,232.2mn vs consensus $2,220.6mn (+1%), a different revenue basis.

3Q26 segment adjusted operating income: LTL $58.9mn vs GS $73.5mn (-20%) and consensus $75.7mn, Truckload $100.0mn vs GS $110.6mn, Logistics $49.4mn vs GS $48.5mn. Total adjusted operating income $194.2mn vs GS $212.7mn and consensus EBIT $207.8mn.
3Q26 total adjusted operating ratio 89.5% vs GS 88.6%. The consensus table shows OR of 91.3% vs consensus 90.6%.
4Q26 EPS guidance $1.30-$1.40 vs GS prior forecast $1.60 and consensus $1.63. GS 4Q26E EPS in the forecast table is $1.35.
Medium-term normalized OR targets previously given by management: LTL 80-85%, Truckload 82-86%, Logistics 86-88%.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS says a firmer manufacturing environment would help LTL density and margin. If ISM turned up further while TFI could not improve margin or handle volume in US LTL, that would raise concern.

risk_factors: Freight downturn tied to the economy.
M&A reliance affecting growth predictability, and acquisition integration issues.
Inability to improve LTL operations and margin.
Potential tariff impact and USMCA negotiations.
Volatility in the broader transport market.
If manufacturing turns up and TFI cannot improve margin or handle volume in US LTL, concern would rise.
geopolitical: USMCA negotiations and potential tariff impact are listed as downside risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Logistics and Truckload are performing well, flatbed exposure is strong, 4Q26 LTL OR is guided to improve 40-140bps sequentially as 3PL surge costs exit, and management is bringing in an outside manager. GS keeps Buy with 37.7% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: LTL yields are down 1% ex-fuel, costs remain elevated, the 4Q guide is below consensus, LTL OR is guided to worsen 0-100bps y/y, and GS sees margin under pressure in 1H27 plus the UPS GFP revenue loss in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If manufacturing (ISM) turns up further and TFI cannot improve margin and/or handle an uptick in volume in US LTL, concern would rise.

theme_stances.key_argument: GS needs more visibility on the timing and pace of the LTL turnaround before it is comfortable with TFI's longer-term growth path.
theme_stances.evidence: we will need greater visibility as to timing and pace of the LTL turnaround
